author: Amr
subject: ci: auto-merge main → gh-pages when all CI is green (Pages-deploy only) (#400)
body:
* ci: auto-merge main → gh-pages when all CI is green (Pages-deploy only)

Replaces the manual "Merge main into gh-pages" PRs with an automatic gate.

deploy-gh-pages.yml triggers on the completion of the push-to-main CI
workflows (CodeQL runs on every main push, so a signal always fires),
re-reads ALL check-runs + commit statuses for that exact commit, and merges
the *validated* SHA into gh-pages only when nothing is pending and nothing
failed. Idempotent (skips if gh-pages already contains the SHA), serialized
via concurrency, bounded poll for stragglers.

Only the built-in GitHub Pages build runs on the gh-pages push:
- every push-triggered workflow is now scoped to main/master
  (validate-solutions.yml was the only branchless one — now guarded);
- the push uses the default GITHUB_TOKEN, which does not trigger further
  Actions runs, while the legacy Pages build (a Pages-service job) still
  fires on the branch update.

No CI is re-run for the merge; gh-pages is source and Pages builds it.

- Relax the job `if` to react to any CI completion on main/master (push,

  gates make extra triggers safe, and a commit left pending when an earlier
  run timed out now gets re-evaluated on the next CI signal instead of being
  stranded until the next push.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): repair invalid quest-perfection workflow + guard workflow validity (#402)
body:
* fix(ci): repair invalid quest-perfection workflow + guard workflow validity

quest-perfection.yml was an *invalid workflow file*: the `fix` job (a
reusable-workflow call) read `matrix.open_new_fix_prs` in its job-level
`if`, but `matrix` is not an available context there (only github, inputs,
needs, vars are). GitHub can't parse it, so it emitted a 0-job failed run
on every push to any branch since #394 introduced it — pushes re-validate
all workflows, so one broken file reddened unrelated branches.

Fix: apply the per-entry gate UPSTREAM. The `plan` job now emits a
pre-filtered `fix_matrix`/`fix_count` holding only the slices granted a fix
PR (open_new_fix_prs == "true"); the `fix` job fans out over that with a
plain needs-based `if`. Semantics are unchanged — all slices still get
walked; only granted ones get a fix PR — and the empty-grant case sets
fix_count=0 so the job skips cleanly (no empty-matrix error).

Add lint-workflows.yml: runs actionlint on the workflow files a PR CHANGES
(shellcheck off — this gates validity, not shell style) so this class of
error is caught in review instead of after merge. Verified it flags the
exact `matrix` error on #394's pre-fix content. Scoped to changed files so
pre-existing style noise in untouched workflows never blocks an unrelated
PR. actionlint + image pinned by version/digest per repo convention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: ci: replace deploy-gh-pages gate with a routine main→gh-pages PR sync (#403)
body:
PR #400 merged the workflow_run-based gate, which was too convoluted. Replace
it with a simple scheduled workflow: every 6h (or on demand) it checks whether
main is ahead of gh-pages and fully green, then opens a PR main→gh-pages and
merges it. GitHub Pages builds gh-pages — the only run on the update.

- Reads main's already-finished CI (no reruns, no waiting on workflow_run).
- gh-pages is now a clean mirror of main (reconciled out-of-band), so the PR
  never conflicts; the step also waits for mergeability and bails on conflict.
- Merge via GITHUB_TOKEN + main/master-scoped workflows => no CI on the push.

Removes deploy-gh-pages.yml. Keeps the validate-solutions guard (already on
main) and #402's lint-workflows.yml / quest-perfection fix untouched.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: ci: remove defunct PRD Machine sync workflow (#404)
body:
The check-conflicts job declared `needs: sync` while its `if` read
`needs.check.outputs.needs_update`. Because `check` was not in its `needs`,
`needs.check` resolved to null, the condition was always false, and the job
was silently skipped on every run (actionlint: property "check" is not
defined in object type {sync: ...}).

Rather than reactivate it, remove the whole workflow. The PRD Machine v2
sync job has never produced a PR and PRD.md has never been auto-updated;
the conflict-detection path only ever auto-opened ~30 "Requirement
Conflicts Detected" issues (Mar-Apr 2026, all since closed) before this bug
silently disabled it. Reactivating would resurrect that issue spam, counter
to the repo's move away from advisory issue noise.

Also drop the now-dangling prd-sync.yml row from the workflows index. The
prd-machine script, PRD.md, and docs are left in place.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): unbreak the quest-perfection loop's startup failure (#422)
body:
Every scheduled run of quest-perfection.yml since 2026-07-01 died as a
startup_failure: the `fix` caller job granted no permissions, so the
nested quest-fix.yml `fix` job's contents:write + pull-requests:write
request exceeded the workflow-level contents:read cap and GitHub
rejected the whole workflow graph at trigger time — before even the
gate job ran. Grant the caller job exactly what the called workflow
requests.

Also repair two issues the first successful run would have hit next:

- Artifact names reject '/', but the slice job named its artifact
  quest-perfection-<char>/<code>. Carry a dashed branch_slug in the
  plan matrix and use it for the artifact AND the report-PR branch
  (consistent with the fix lane's automated/quest-fix-<char>-<code>).
- The orchestrator never passed the walk's plan/evidence artifacts to
  quest-fix, so the fix lane would re-derive evidence with a second
  expensive agentic execute run — and repair a DIFFERENT run's findings
  than the walkthrough report the human reviews. Pass the slice
  artifact through plan_artifact/evidence_artifact (quest-fix still
  re-derives anything the artifact doesn't contain).

Validated with actionlint 1.7.12 at CI parity and a local simulation
of the plan job's matrix step (branch_slug present, fix_matrix filter
intact, dashed character keys handled).

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(ci): workflow-minted sealed quest evidence, one consolidated report PR, dispatch-only standalone walkthrough (#433)
body:
* fix(ci): mint quest-walk evidence deterministically — seal it, consolidate the report PR, retire the duplicate daily walkthrough

The loop's first real run (28704852428) proved the orchestration works
but exposed a systemic flaw: the agentic execute engine was invoked
INSIDE the quest-walker/quest-fixer agents, and Claude Code scrubs
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from Bash-tool subprocess
environments — so the engine's child `claude` processes always
auth-aborted, the walker hand-wrote evidence (on 07-03 even an
in-schema file with executed=true), the ledger refused to certify, and
every fix lane M7-aborted. Safe, but sterile: the loop could walk
forever and never fix anything.

Three changes, per the loop's own workflow-not-agent doctrine:

1. Workflow-minted, SEALED evidence. The engine now runs as a
   deterministic `run:` step (the job env carries auth, so its
   children authenticate) in quest-perfection's slice job,
   quest-walkthrough, and quest-fix's re-derive path (whose gather
   agent step is deleted outright). walk-plan.json + walk-evidence.*
   are snapshotted to $RUNNER_TEMP before any agent runs and restored
   after — an agent can read evidence but a hand-rolled copy can never
   reach the ledger, the artifact, or the fix lane. The slice job also
   drops to contents:read and loses the PAT from its env.

2. ONE consolidated report PR per run. Per-slice PRs each carried a
   sibling .quests/ledger.json delta cut from the same base — merging

author: Amr
subject: fix(quests): rotate a bounded quest window per run + accumulate coverage across days (#438)
body:
* fix(quests): rotate a bounded quest window per run + accumulate coverage across days

The first scheduled run of the perfection loop against main (28739367908)
auth-failed 5 of 6 slices: the loop planned EVERY quest in a level (26 for
developer/0001) and ran the engine over all of them, so a single run walked
~109 quests across 3h17m and exhausted the OAuth token's rate limit
("could not authenticate" AFTER 9 successful quests — a throttle, not the
scrub bug). Only the 3-quest slice survived.

Cap-and-rotate on the free subscription token (the chosen direction):

- Planner: `--window N` walks a date-ROTATED window of N quests instead of
  the whole level; over ceil(total/N) days the level is swept without gap or
  overlap. `stats.total_quests` carries the full size. `--max-quests` (first-N)
  stays for the manual arm.
- Ledger: accumulate per-quest coverage across runs (`slice.coverage`, keyed
  by quest path; a re-walk overwrites, so a fail→pass fix sticks). `perfect`
  is recomputed over the WHOLE slice — every quest covered, execute-mode,
  passing, fresh (perfect.coverage_days=21) — NOT on one all-pass window. The
  circuit breaker only advances on a FULLY-COVERED-but-imperfect walk, so a
  mid-sweep run is progress, not a failed fix round. Dashboard gains a Cov
  (covered/total) column; the report PR table shows window + coverage.
- Engine: a mid-batch auth throttle now writes PARTIAL evidence + exits 0 if
  ≥1 quest scored (the completed quests still count as coverage…

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): unbreak the auto-merge lanes — stop watching our own check (#441)
body:
Every auto-merge workflow (dependabot, content, issue) ran
`gh pr checks "$PR" --watch --fail-fast`, which blocks until EVERY
check on the PR reaches a terminal state — including the auto-merge
job's OWN check, which stays 'pending' for exactly as long as it is
doing the watching. That is a self-deadlock: the watch never returns,
the job hits timeout-minutes (30), and the PR is left unmerged with a
failed 'auto-merge' check. Confirmed in the logs: all functional checks
(actionlint, CodeQL, Analyze ×3) show 'pass' while 'auto-merge pending 0'
is the run watching itself, then 'The operation was canceled.' at 30m.
Every Dependabot PR (#373/#374/#412/#413) sat unmerged this way, and the
content lane — which is supposed to squash-merge the quest-perfection
fix PRs — has the same latent bug.

Replace --watch with a poll loop that excludes our own run (its check
link carries $GITHUB_RUN_ID), so it waits only on checks that can
actually finish. A hard failure still stops the merge (label ci-failed);
'pending' waits; all-green merges; 'only self so far' waits rather than
merging unchecked. Same fix in all three lanes.

Validated: actionlint clean (incl. shellcheck); the decision logic
unit-tested against #413's real check data (self excluded → pass ×5 +
skipping ×2 → MERGE) and synthetic fail/pending/green/only-self rows.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat(quests): harden quest-perfection loop + surface walkthroughs/ledger on the site (#471)
body:
* feat(quests): harden quest-perfection loop + surface walkthroughs/ledger on the site

Two cohesive bodies of work on the ♾️ quest-perfection loop.

## 1. Loop reliability (fixes the run-29190829265 red X)
A transient first-quest auth/rate-limit blip was throwing away a whole slice and
reddening the run (5 sibling slices passed with the same token seconds later).

- runner.py: bounded retry-with-backoff+jitter for the recoverable classes
  (overload/429/529/5xx/network + ambiguous auth blips), gated on a non-clean exit
  so a clean transcript mentioning "503" isn't retried. Timeouts fail fast.
  Sustained throttle → AuthError (batch-stop). Env-tunable; pinned by test_retry_policy.
- quest-perfection.yml: drop `xargs` (it masks the engine exit code to 123) →
  `mapfile`; soft-skip an exit-2 rate-limit truncation (warning, not red; skip the
  walker since it shares the throttled token) while a real crash still fails loudly.
  The report job now hard-fails only on a WHOLE-SWEEP wipeout (0/N slices scored),
  so a broken token can't hide behind all-green warnings.

## 2. Surface the output on the site + auto-merge (review on the frontend, not the PR)
- scripts/quest/build_reports_site.py: deterministic generator turning the raw

* fix(quests): repair verified walkthrough issues [system-engineer/0101]

* fix(quests): guard LaTeX code block with raw tags in lazytex CV quest

The Jekyll Build Test failed with a Liquid syntax error:

The CV starter's LaTeX \newcommand definition contains '{%'

interprets as an unterminated tag even inside a fenced code block.

author: Amr
subject: ci(quest-perfection): isolate slice failures so a partial sweep still counts (#509)
body:
One failed matrix leg (a transient 'Set up job' action-resolution 500, or a
single engine hiccup) was marking the entire multi-hour daily run as failed,
booking ~700 productive minutes per fortnight as waste even when 5/6 slices
succeeded.

- slice job: continue-on-error so a failed leg no longer sets the run
  conclusion (job-level, so it also absorbs pre-step 'Set up job' infra
  errors no in-job retry can reach); legs stay visibly red in the UI
- slice job: timeout-minutes 45 so a stuck agentic engine can't run toward
  the 6h ceiling
- report job: new 'Surface failed slices' step — warns per undelivered
  slice (annotation + step summary) and hard-fails the run only on a
  sweep-wide wipeout, so total failure stays loud
- setup-python: cache pip on plan/slice/report

Addresses bamr87/bamr87#23

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: ci(dependabot): merge workflow-file bumps with an elevated PAT and recover from stale-branch races (#510)
body:
The auto-merger merged with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, which cannot merge
PRs that modify .github/workflows/** ("refusing to allow a GitHub App to
create or update workflow ... without `workflows` permission"). Since
github_actions-ecosystem bumps inherently touch workflow files, every
such PR waited the full check-poll and then failed at mergePullRequest
(e.g. PR #506 / run 29516380107) — 85% wasted minutes, 11% effective.

- Merge with AUTO_PR_GITHUB_TOKEN || PAT_TOKEN || GITHUB_TOKEN (the same
  elevated-token fallback chain the quest-* and content-factory
  workflows already use); polling/labeling stays on least-privilege
  GITHUB_TOKEN.
- If a bump touches .github/workflows/** and no PAT is configured, skip
  the 25-minute wait entirely: label manual-merge-required, comment why,
  exit green.
- If the merge loses a stale-branch race to a sibling PR, comment
  "@dependabot rebase" and exit; the rebase push re-triggers this
  workflow (synchronize) and the fresh run merges.
- If the merge is still rejected for workflow scope (expired/mis-scoped
  PAT), label + comment + fail loudly instead of dying blind.

Fixes the failure mode reported in bamr87/bamr87#26.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: ci: reduce Actions waste — consolidate auto-merge trio, path-filter CodeQL, halve sync cadence, drop dead workflows (#511)
body:
Implements the audited CI-waste plan for it-journey (post PR #509/#510,
which already fixed ~98% of the wasted minutes; this pass removes the
remaining run noise and inert machinery).

* content-auto-merge.yml — SURVIVOR of the auto-merge consolidation.
  Absorbs issue-pr-auto-merge.yml (auto:issue policy: same-repo
  provenance + content-only + resolver allow-globs pages/**, assets/**,
  _data/quests/**) and quest-report-auto-merge.yml (automated +
  quest-walkthrough policy: allow-globs pages/_quest-reports/**,
  .quests/**, test/quest-validator/walkthroughs/**) as a label→policy
  table. One run per PR event instead of three (~250 mostly-skipped
  runs/14d → ~83). The poll-for-green loop is KEPT, not replaced with
  `gh pr merge --auto`: main has no branch protection and no rulesets
  (branches/main/protection → 404, rules/branches/main → []), so
  --auto would merge instantly without waiting on checks.

* issue-pr-auto-merge.yml, quest-report-auto-merge.yml — deleted
  (merged into the survivor; per-policy gates, scopes, and vars
  preserved verbatim).

* codeql-analysis.yml — paths-ignore (pages/**, **/*.md, _data/**,
  assets/images/**) on push + pull_request; weekly cron unchanged for
  full-coverage scans. ~2/3 of its 64.5 min/14d scanned commits that
  touch no code. Est. ~40 min/14d saved.

* sync-gh-pages.yml — cron 20 */6 * * * → 20 2,14 * * * (after the
  daytime bot-merge window and after evening dependabot merges).
  ~58% of 6-hourly syncs no-oped; halves runs,…

The one-paragraph-per-line check scans the whole repo. The quest-perfection
loop emits soft-wrapped prose into pages/_quest-reports/ and

subject: PostHog analytics: instrument Ruby SEO/content scripts (#517)
body:
* PostHog analytics: instrument Ruby SEO/content scripts

Add optional, token-gated PostHog event capture to the four Ruby SEO/content
scripts so script activity and content health can be tracked over time. When
POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN is unset the scripts skip analytics entirely — no client,
no network call, identical behavior and exit codes — so CI without the secret
is unaffected.

Events (all distinct_id 'it-journey-ci'):
- content_scan_completed            (content-freshness-check.rb)
- ctr_report_generated / gsc_csv_parsed (ctr-report-generator.rb)
- frontmatter_validation_completed  (frontmatter-validator.rb)
- statistics_generated              (generate_statistics.rb)

Each uses the instance-based PostHog::Client, captures before any exit(), and
calls shutdown in an ensure block so buffered events flush.

Also:
- Gemfile/Gemfile.lock: add posthog-ruby (~> 3.19). Kept BUNDLED WITH at
  2.3.25 (the wizard had bumped it to 4.0.11, which would change the bundler
  CI installs via ruby/setup-ruby).
- .env.example: document POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN and POSTHOG_HOST.
- docs/setup/POSTHOG_ANALYTICS.md: integration + verification notes.
- .claude/skills/integration-ruby: PostHog Ruby agent skill for future work.

Verified: all 5 events fire with correct payloads against a local mock
ingestion server; no-token path sends nothing and does not touch the network;

builds.

  as M2's `make quest-data`. Verified against PR #534's two failing files.
- Skills (content-curator, quest-forge, cms-curator, quest-fix): add the
  one-paragraph-per-line rule + `make prose-oneline-apply` to their verify steps
  so the agent-opens-PR workflows comply too.

subject: fix(pages): unbreak the site build; split the quest loop into walk + fix lanes (#572)
body:
* ci(claude): serialize @claude runs per issue/PR thread

claude.yml was the only workflow in this repo without a concurrency group.
Several @claude mentions in quick succession each spun up their own
30-minute agent against the same thread, racing each other on the same
branch.

Deliberately NOT cancel-in-progress: each mention is a distinct request
and the agent commits and pushes, so a superseded run is queued behind
the current one rather than killed mid-push.

This back-fills the fix made in bamr87/bamr87 templates/agent-context/
(kit 0.2.0). The kit is additive-only and never overwrites an existing
claude.yml, so repos already carrying a seeded copy — this one included —
do not pick it up via fan-out and need it applied directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LMU2wWXi5Kwj267ChmJqpe

* fix(pages): exclude AGENTS.md from the Jekyll build — it breaks the site

The GitHub Pages build has been hard-failing, so the published site is not
updating. Root cause, from run 30371782351:

  Liquid Exception: Liquid syntax error (line 180): Tag '{% %}' was not
  properly terminated with regexp: /\%\}/ in AGENTS.md

AGENTS.md:180 documents the `oneline` gate and mentions Liquid `{% %}` in
prose. Jekyll runs Liquid over the RAW file before Markdown, so the
backticks around it do not protect anything — Liquid sees an unterminated
tag and aborts the build.

Fix: exclude AGENTS.md, exactly as CLAUDE.md already is and…
